newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China, Britain reach pact on 96/97 HK land scheme.
newsitem.headline: China, Britain reach pact on 96/97 HK land scheme.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Monday China and Britain agreed to double the amount of crown land disposable in the current fiscal year ending March 31.

The two sides, working closely in the run-up to China's takeover of Hong Kong in mid-1997, sealed an agreement on adjustments in the British-ruled territory's land disposal programme for the year, a government statement said.
Under an accord secured at a meeting of the Sino-British Land Commission, a total of 157.16 hectares of land will be disposed of this year in addition to 153 hectares agreed in May.

The extra land includes 70.19 hectares for the development of Container Terminal Nine, 76.40 hectares for track and related facilities for the Chek Lap Kok airport railway and an additional 1.66 hectares for the railway's Hong Kong station.

Development of Container Terminal Nine was held up for four years by Chinese objections to the way the contract was awarded and to the presence of Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd group in the consortium until Britain and China reached agreement in September to allow the project to proceed.
Hong Kong is building a railway to link the new airport, scheduled to be operational in 1998, with other parts of the territory.
China and Britain also agreed that the average cost of land production -- improvements in land to make it more marketable -- for 1996/97 would be HK$5,480 per square metre.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese control at midnight on June 30, 1997.
